apps.name: 420 Wallet
apps.purpose: Native wallet, accounts, assets, validator controls, dApp access, notifications

apps.name: 420 Explorer
apps.purpose: Blocks, transactions, contracts, validators, assets, governance, finality

apps.name: 420 Registry
apps.purpose: Canonical registry of contracts, tokens, applications and protocol services

apps.name: 420 Names
apps.purpose: Human-readable names such as crowley.420 layered over canonical identities

apps.name: 420 Identity
apps.purpose: Optional decentralized identity, profiles, credentials and reputation

apps.name: 420 Stake
apps.purpose: Validator registration, 42,000 420 bond, credit, readiness, lifecycle, rewards and withdrawals; no stake-weighted delegation at genesis

apps.name: 420 Governance
apps.purpose: Community House, Validator House, proposals, voting, treasury and timelock

apps.name: 420 AI
apps.purpose: AI providers, models, jobs, escrow, payments and reputation; no consensus privilege

apps.name: 420 Attention
apps.purpose: Opt-in Cannaseur campaigns and attention rewards

apps.name: 420 Status
apps.purpose: Network, finality, validator, RPC, bridge, swap and AI service health

apps.name: 420 Faucet
apps.purpose: Testnet distribution and developer onboarding; no monetary value

rules: Front ends are not consensus-critical and may be upgraded independently.
420 Registry is the canonical discovery backbone.
420 Names never replaces canonical protocol/service identity.
420 Stake does not include stake-weighted delegation at genesis.
420 Attention cannot access wallet keys, auto-sign, execute arbitrary wallet code, or transact on behalf of users.
420 Faucet never participates in mainnet genesis economics.
